dedupe_keys.name: dessim district energy systems simulation open source python toolbox on pypsa for simulating and optimising buildings on heating and chilled water networks

description: DESsim, for District Energy Systems simulation, is an open-source set of Python modules from the engineering studio Elioth, part of the Egis group, for simulating and optimising the energy systems of buildings connected to district heating and chilled water networks. The announcement read on 2026-09-28, published in November 2020, explains that it builds on the open PyPSA power system library, takes its inputs from geographic information system data, and is designed to explore many design scenarios; Elioth used it on urban projects including the Bruneseau district, and a EuroSun 2020 paper applies it to a fictitious French mixed-use district, comparing a design that minimises greenhouse gas emissions with one that minimises energy cost and showing annual flows as a Sankey diagram. The article says the tool is free on GitLab, documented and open to contributions, and that some calculations still need improvement. Coverage is not geographic. Access is free; the repository and its licence were not opened. Caveats: the announcement is from 2020 and current maintenance is unknown. It supports optimisation and planning studies, such as sizing a shared heat and cold loop for a new district and comparing carbon and cost designs. Related record: the chilled water plant simulator.
